subject.title: Bug: Built-in dreaming system contaminates agent identity in multi-agent setups

question: Should memory-core dreaming enforce agent isolation by default for agents sharing a workspace, or should maintainers accept an explicit dreaming agent allowlist/config contract as the supported boundary?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but the permanent boundary affects security defaults, plugin config surface, SDK helper shape, persisted artifact cleanup, and upgrade behavior, so automation should not choose the product/security contract alone.

options.title: Default Agent Isolation
options.body: Treat multi-agent docs as the contract and make dreaming use only the current agent's transcripts and artifacts unless cross-agent sharing is explicitly configured.

options.title: Accept Allowlist Contract
options.body: Land a documented `dreaming.agents` or equivalent allowlist as the first supported control while keeping stronger default isolation tracked separately.

options.title: Document Workspace Pooling
options.body: Declare shared-workspace dreaming as expected behavior and document that operators must use separate workspaces or gateways for isolation.

recommendation.title: Default Agent Isolation
recommendation.body: Treat multi-agent docs as the contract and make dreaming use only the current agent's transcripts and artifacts unless cross-agent sharing is explicitly configured.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned, narrowed the bug in public comments, and have recent history in the affected dreaming resolver and docs surface.
